description: The autonomy.grant refusal for a local subject (S56 T6, the -31833 family): a local action runs without a grant — its effects are confined to the working tree, so granting one is a no-op with a confusing audit row. The validator refuses it with the pure sentence rather than storing a row that could never be exercised. The subject is a REAL registry name, which is what makes this refusal distinct from unknown-subject: the name exists, the class is wrong.

data.what: git.createBranch is local — it runs without a grant
data.means: a grant is a human-authored authority record with closed rules (subject, conditions, expiry, the node it may sit on); a request outside them is refused, not silently corrected — nothing was written
data.todo: the refusal names the rule it broke and the thing it broke it on; `autonomy.vocabulary` lists the closed sets a request may name
